scenario.title: 跟朋友介紹新同事、新室友
scenario.context: 「他人很好」「她很有趣」「那個人很煩」——描述一個人是聊天最常見的題材。英文有一整組 -ed / -ing 形容詞，用錯了會從「我覺得很無聊」變成「我是個無聊的人」。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: So what's the new guy on your team like?
lines.zh: 所以你們組上那個新人怎麼樣？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Daniel? He's really down-to-earth. Super easy to talk to.
lines.zh: Daniel 嗎？他人很實在，超好聊。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: That's good. Is he any good at his job?

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Yeah, he's a total tech nerd. Ask him anything about computers.
lines.zh: 好啊，他是超級科技宅，電腦的事問他就對了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Better than the last guy, then.

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Way better. The last guy was a pain in the neck. He complained about everything.
lines.zh: 好太多了。上一個超煩，什麼都要抱怨。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: I remember. You always looked so annoyed after meetings with him.
lines.zh: 我記得，你每次跟他開完會都一臉厭煩。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Because those meetings were so annoying!
lines.zh: 因為那些會議真的很煩啊！

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: How was the date last night?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: Honestly? I was bored after twenty minutes.
lines.zh: 老實說？二十分鐘後我就覺得無聊了。

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: Not boring exactly. He just talked about crypto the whole time.
lines.zh: 也不算無聊，他只是整晚都在講加密貨幣。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Ha, so he's interested in money. Is he interesting, though?
lines.zh: 哈，所以他對錢有興趣。那他人有趣嗎？

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: Not really. I prefer someone more laid-back.
lines.zh: 不太有趣。我比較喜歡隨和一點的人。

patterns.note: 問個性；What does he look like? 才是問外表

patterns.en: She's really easy to talk to.
He's a bit shy at first, but he's really funny.
patterns.zh: 他一開始有點害羞，但其實很好笑。

patterns.en: She's the kind of person who ___.

patterns.note: 第 31 單元會正式學這個俚語

patterns.en: He's tall, with short curly hair.
I'm not a big fan of him.
patterns.note: 比 I don't like him 委婉

patterns.en: She's got a great sense of humor.

chinglish.why: I'm boring 是「我是個無聊的人」。要說「我覺得無聊」用 bored。

chinglish.wrong: He is a very nice guy, very kind, very good.
chinglish.why: 中文習慣疊一串「很好、很善良」。英文用一兩個精準的形容詞，再舉一個例子，描述會更有畫面。
look like 後面接的是 what，How 和 like 不能同時出現。問個性就用 What's he like?

chinglish.wrong: She is very interesting in art.
chinglish.why: 「對…有興趣」用 interested in；interesting 是「令人感興趣的」。

grammar.title: -ed / -ing 形容詞
grammar.oneLiner: -ed 描述「人的感受」，-ing 描述「造成這種感受的人事物」。
whenToUse: -ed：我感到…。I'm bored / interested / tired / excited / confused / annoyed.
-ing：它（或他）讓人感到…。The movie is boring. / He's interesting. / This is confusing.
形容人時兩種都能用，但意思完全不同：He's bored（他覺得無聊）vs He's boring（他這個人很無聊）。
常見組合：bored/boring, interested/interesting, excited/exciting, tired/tiring, confused/confusing, annoyed/annoying, embarrassed/embarrassing, surprised/surprising。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文的「無聊」「有趣」「煩」同時可以指感受和原因：「我好無聊」「這部片好無聊」用同一個詞。英文卻要看主詞是「感受者」還是「原因」。台灣人最經典的錯誤就是 I'm so boring，本來想說「我好無聊喔」，結果變成「我是個很無聊的人」。

examples.correct: I was so bored during the meeting.
examples.incorrect: I was so boring during the meeting.

examples.note: 對某事有興趣用 interested in。

examples.correct: I'm confused. Can you explain it again?
examples.incorrect: I'm confusing. Can you explain it again?

quiz.question: There's nothing to do. I'm so ___.
His explanation was really ___. I didn't understand anything.
I tripped in front of my boss. It was so ___.
After a twelve-hour shift, I'm completely ___ (tire).
quiz.explanation: 描述自己的感受用 tired。

slang.usage: 稱讚一個人不擺架子、很真誠，特別是有名或有成就的人。

risk.note: 正面稱讚，任何場合都能用。

examples.en: For a CEO, she's surprisingly down-to-earth.
examples.zh: 以執行長來說，她意外地很親民。

examples.en: I like him because he's so down-to-earth.
examples.zh: 我喜歡他，因為他很實在。

slang.usage: 形容人的個性或地方的氛圍：a laid-back guy / a laid-back town。

risk.note: 通常是稱讚；但在工作評價裡說某人 too laid-back 可能暗示他不夠積極。

examples.en: My new boss is really laid-back. She doesn't micromanage.
examples.zh: 我新主管很隨和，不會事事緊盯。

examples.en: Tainan has a much more laid-back vibe than Taipei.
examples.zh: 台南的氣氛比台北悠閒多了。

slang.meaning: 討厭鬼、很麻煩的人或事
slang.usage: 形容讓人很煩的人或事情。

risk.note: 私下抱怨可以；當面說某人是 a pain in the neck 很傷人。更粗俗的版本 a pain in the ass 職場絕對避免。

examples.en: Filling out these forms is a pain in the neck.
My neighbor's kid can be a real pain in the neck.
examples.zh: 我鄰居的小孩有時候很煩人。

slang.meaning: 書呆子、某領域的狂熱者、宅
slang.usage: 現在常常是中性甚至正面的意思：a design nerd / a coffee nerd（對某事很懂很熱衷的人）。

risk.note: 自稱沒問題；說別人時語氣要友善，否則可能被當成嘲笑對方不合群。

examples.en: I'm a total font nerd. I can talk about typefaces for hours.
examples.zh: 我是字體宅，可以聊字體聊好幾個小時。

examples.en: Ask Tom. He's the computer nerd in our office.
examples.zh: 問 Tom，他是我們辦公室的電腦通。

review.question: Has the plumber come ___?
review.explanation: 複習第 12 單元：問句用 yet。

review.question: My laptop has been acting ___ all week.
review.explanation: 複習第 12 單元：act up = 出毛病。

review.question: There ___ a lot of noise from upstairs last night.
review.explanation: 複習第 11 單元：noise 不可數，用 was。

review.question: I ___ my dentist at 3 tomorrow. It's already booked.
review.explanation: 複習第 9 單元：已排定的行程用進行式。

review.question: Can you give me some ___?
review.explanation: 複習第 5 單元：advice 不可數。

review.question: Which one means "我好無聊"?
review.explanation: 感受用 bored；I'm boring 是「我是個無聊的人」。
